\begin{table}[tbp]
  \caption{Framework selection: a representative selection taken from the first author's thesis~\citep{thakur2026thesis}, neither exhaustive nor the best. Top: the four frameworks we studied, with the interface as we ran them. Bottom: the six excluded frameworks, each with the reason and, in italics, the criterion it did not meet.}
  \label{tab:frameworks}
  \footnotesize
  \begin{tabular}{@{}p{0.15\columnwidth}p{0.17\columnwidth}p{0.11\columnwidth}p{0.42\columnwidth}@{}}
    \toprule
    Framework & Interface & Model & Design scope \\
    \midrule
    Flask & WSGI & sync & micro-framework \\
    Django & WSGI & sync & full-stack framework \\
    FastAPI & ASGI & async & API-oriented framework \\
    Tornado & \raggedright native event loop & async & web framework and\newline networking library \\
    \midrule
    Excluded & \multicolumn{3}{p{0.79\columnwidth}@{}}{Reason (\emph{criterion not met})} \\
    \midrule
    Bottle & \multicolumn{3}{p{0.79\columnwidth}@{}}{A small WSGI micro-framework~\citep{bottledocs} overlapping Flask in this selection (\emph{architectural distinctness})} \\
    Pyramid & \multicolumn{3}{p{0.79\columnwidth}@{}}{A synchronous WSGI framework, the category of Flask and Django (\emph{architectural distinctness})} \\
    Falcon & \multicolumn{3}{p{0.79\columnwidth}@{}}{An API framework for WSGI and ASGI, two interfaces that Flask, Django and FastAPI already cover (\emph{interface diversity})} \\
    Starlette & \multicolumn{3}{p{0.79\columnwidth}@{}}{The ASGI toolkit beneath FastAPI, a second ASGI entry (\emph{interface diversity})} \\
    Sanic & \multicolumn{3}{p{0.79\columnwidth}@{}}{Like Tornado, a native event-loop server, a slot the selection already fills; its built-in server uses uvloop by default on supported platforms~\citep{sanicdocs}, whereas both async servers here ran on the standard asyncio loop; an untested alternative (\emph{interface diversity})} \\
    aiohttp & \multicolumn{3}{p{0.79\columnwidth}@{}}{An asyncio HTTP client and server with routing and middleware, whose server would fill the native event-loop slot of Tornado (\emph{architectural distinctness})} \\
    \bottomrule
  \end{tabular}
\end{table}
